facts.title: A back turned to the infinite
facts.body: Friedrich’s Wanderer above the Sea of Fog (c. 1818) places a solitary Rückenfigur on a rock — we see what he sees, and we do not see his face.

facts.title: The anonymous witness
facts.body: Seen from behind, the wanderer becomes a stand-in for the viewer — Romantic contemplation as a shared stance.

facts.title: A sea that is not water
facts.body: Fog fills the valleys like a pale ocean — landscape as weather of the soul.

facts.title: A precarious perch
facts.body: Sharp rock underfoot makes the sublime feel unstable — beauty with an edge.

facts.title: Islands in the mist
facts.body: Distant ridges pierce the fog like islands — depth measured in vanishing greens and greys.

facts.title: Dark against the pale
facts.body: The dark coat silhouettes the figure cleanly against mist — a single human ink blot on vast air.

facts.title: A stick for the climb
facts.body: The walking stick hints at a journey already made — arrival, not departure.

facts.title: Light without sun
facts.body: The sky is bright yet sourceless — illumination as atmosphere rather than ray.
